result.reason: The clause gives Company a 30-day written-notice right, including during an active Statement of Work, with a refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period. Contractor may terminate only between engagements on 90 days’ notice, so it cannot terminate during a committed Statement of Work. However, allowing Company to terminate a Statement of Work “in part” goes beyond the playbook and may alter pricing or scope-allocation economics; that expansion is unnecessary and does not fully preserve unrelated commercial intent. The refund wording is workable, though expressly stating that the refund is pro rata would be clearer.
